title: Rav Hamnuna the Elder
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Pesachim 105a: Rav Chananya bar Shelamya and Rav’s students were sitting at a meal, and Rav Hamnuna the Elder was standing over them. They said to him: “Go see whether the day has been sanctified; we will stop and establish the meal for Shabbat.” He said to them: “You need not; Shabbat establishes its own obligation, for Rav said,” etc. Rav Amram said to them, etc.

In Sukkah 42a and Gittin 39b: “Rav Shmuel bar Chatai said that Rav Hamnuna the Elder said that Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ashyan said that Rav Huna said.” In Ketubot 40a: “Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbah bar Shila said that Rav Hamnuna the Elder said that Rav Ada bar Ahavah said”; Hyman proposes the same reading in Gittin 26b. In Gittin 81a: “Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbah bar She’ilta said that Rav Hamnuna the Elder said that Rav Ada bar Ahavah said.” There is also a Rav Hamnuna the Elder mentioned in the Zohar several times; see Seder HaDorot.

notes.text: The meal-setting language concerns Shabbat establishing its obligation; the quotation is abridged and no response for Rav Amram is invented. The Zohar notice is retained separately without automatically identifying its Hamnuna with this one.

The consulted Pesachim 105a distinguishes Shabbat establishing the Kiddush obligation from Havdalah. This comparison does not supply the omitted Rav Amram quotation or establish identity with a Zohar namesake.
